newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil firms on French demand, barges dul.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil firms on French demand, barges dul.

text.p: NWE gas oil cargo premiums firmed around $2 on steady demand in sluggish business on Monday and buyer resistance put pressure on barge premiums, traders said.
Benchmark Feb IPE gas oil futures ended down $6.75 at $209 a tonne on warmer weather in northern Europe.
A cargo of French grade heating oil sold for Feb +$8 for February 1-10 delivery cif Le Havre, $2 firmer.

A trader added a notional $4 to premiums by bidding Feb +$12 and then $14 into Bordeaux but failed to attract a suitable size. Prompt Russians were steady at Feb IPE +$7.50 cif NWE. German winter grade prompt was around Feb IPE +$10/12 cif NWE.

Demand emerged for 20,000 tonne parcels of low sulphur diesel into Le Havre but found no selling interest. Smaller Russian quality parcels were seen as unsuitable. The arb out of NWE was closed. Traders said the only arb to the region was possibly from the Med but it looked marginal.
Slack German demand pressured barges. Prompt Rotterdam refinery heating oil was around Feb +$8/9.50 fob ARA.
Feburary dates were offered at Feb IPE +$5, down $1. Heating oil for Antwerp was down at Feb IPE +$5 fob ARA. Demand was flat for low sulphur diesel, notionally around Feb IPE +$12/13.
